scenarios.title: Sluggish adoption
scenarios.text: Wisconsin performs like the slowest statewide reforms so far, Rhode Island and Oregon.
scenarios.info: The average of the two slowest statewide-law states, Rhode Island (0.62) and Oregon (0.68): about 0.65 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year at a typical place once the law is fully in force (4 years or more), with each Wisconsin place adjusted for its home values, incomes and size as in the central scenario. Rhode Island has only one year of data after its law (2025), so its level rests on one year. In 2027–2029 the addition reaches 0.61, 0.78, 0.81 of its full size; full from 2030. No Wisconsin place goes below a minimum rate set from Madison's own permits (0.2345 per 1,000 single-family homes per year: Madison's 2022–2025 rate of 0.1876 divided by 0.8). Madison itself follows the path of similar cities in Washington and Oregon in every scenario.

scenarios.title: Typical adoption after a statewide ADU law
scenarios.description: Typical adoption after a statewide ADU law
scenarios.text: Wisconsin performs like most of the eight states with a statewide ADU law: about 1.00 permit per 1,000 single-family homes per year once the law has been in force 4 years (Washington 1.19, Utah 1.08, Maine 1.00, Vermont 0.90, Massachusetts 0.85). California is one of the eight and counts toward this typical level, yet the level sits far below California's own 2.45.
scenarios.info: The common level of the eight statewide-law states (California included), about 1.00 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year at a typical place once the law has been in force 4 years. Each Wisconsin place is then adjusted for its home values, incomes and size, as places differ within the eight states. In 2027–2029 the addition reaches 0.63, 0.80, 0.82 of its full size; full from 2030. No Wisconsin place goes below a minimum rate set from Madison's own permits (0.2345 per 1,000 single-family homes per year: Madison's 2022–2025 rate of 0.1876 divided by 0.8). Madison itself follows the path of similar cities in Washington and Oregon in every scenario.
scenarios.basis: Like a typical statewide-law state: pooled revision (ii) configuration A central; ramp from the pooled year terms

scenarios.text: Wisconsin does better than every statewide-law state except California: about 1.89 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year once the law has been in force 4 years. Only California has gone higher (2.45), and its laws go beyond the benchmark in several ways (ADUs on apartment properties, more than one ADU per lot), so this is the high end of the expected range.
scenarios.info: The central level times 1.89: the 90th percentile of how much the eight states differ, about 1.89 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year at a typical place. In 2027–2029 the addition reaches 0.64, 0.80, 0.83 of its full size; full from 2030. No Wisconsin place goes below a minimum rate set from Madison's own permits (0.2345 per 1,000 single-family homes per year: Madison's 2022–2025 rate of 0.1876 divided by 0.8). Madison itself follows the path of similar cities in Washington and Oregon in every scenario.
scenarios.basis: Strong adoption: pooled revision (ii) configuration A, 90th percentile of the between-state spread (factor 1.89). The high end of what statewide-law states have reached; only California has gone higher.

reference_line.label: Median performance in 8 examples of statewide ADU reform
reference_line.info: The middle (median) of what the 8 states with a statewide ADU law, California included, actually permitted in each year after their law, applied to Wisconsin's single-family homes. It is a check on the scenarios, not a scenario.
reference_line.detail: Drawn through 2030; 2031 repeats 2030 (dashed, carried forward), because few states have that many years of data yet. ADUs built with a new house on an empty lot are left out (non-California series × 0.951, AQ-039). Rates: 0.75, 0.86, 0.83, 1.18, 1.18 permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year in 2027–2031. Series: reference/pooled_revision_adoption_line.csv (variant vacant_lot_x0.951).
reference_line.why_central_differs: The central scenario (8,721 added permits) and this line (8,208) are built differently. The line applies one median state rate to every Wisconsin home. The central scenario gives each place the level that similar places reached in the eight states (by home values, incomes and size), with a ramp-up in the first three years, and no place below a minimum rate set from Madison's permits.

page_intro.compare: This page shows how many permits for second homes on single-family lots (accessory dwelling units, or ADUs, and conversions of a house into a duplex) Wisconsin can expect if the statewide benchmark ADU law takes effect on 1 January 2027. It shows a baseline of how many would be permitted without the law, and then three scenarios for the bottom, middle and top of what we expect, based on how statewide reform has rolled out in other states. They are scenarios, not confidence intervals: each one describes a way Wisconsin could respond, not a statistical probability.
